questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Since childhood, Monty / ate his food / fast and he / will not change.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb tense in the fourth part of the sentence, 'ate his food', is incorrect.
 
• The sentence describes an ongoing characteristic from childhood to the** present, so the present perfect tense should be used.**
 
• The correct form should be **'has eaten his food'** to indicate the action started in the past and continues to the present.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4)

Correct sentence: *Since childhood, Monty **has eaten his food** fast and he will not change*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• When describing actions or states that began in the past and continue to the present, the present perfect tense is used.
 
 
• **Example:** *She **has lived** in New York since 2010*.
 
 
 
• The present perfect is formed using **'has/have + past participle'** of the verb.
 
 
• Example: *They **have finished** their homework*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

After your insistence, / my sister / checked / a mailbox again.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The phrase **"a mailbox again" **should be corrected to** "the mailbox again" **to make the sentence** grammatically correct.**
 
• The word** "a" **suggests **any mailbox**, whereas **"the" specifies a particular mailbox that is already known to the speaker and listener.**
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be **"the mailbox again".**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *After your insistence, my sister checked** the mailbox **again*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In English grammar, definite and indefinite articles** ("the" and "a" or "an") **are used to indicate specificity or generality respectively.
 
• **"The"** is used when referring to something specific or previously mentioned.
 
• **"A"** or "an" is used when referring to something in a general sense or when it is mentioned for the first time.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

In order to connect / these themes to a wider / historical context, Rahul go / beyond aesthetic analysis.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the third part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb 'go' is incorrect.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject **Rahul** is **singular**.
 
• The verb should agree in number with the subject. Since **Rahul** is singular, the verb should be **goes**.
 
 
• **Example:** *Rahul goes to the market every Sunday.*
 
 
 
• Therefore, the singular form of the verb 'goes' should be used in place of the plural form 'go'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct sentence: *In order to connect these themes to a wider historical context, Rahul** goes** beyond aesthetic analysis*.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part that contains an error.

(A) It is sad / (B) that you / (C) are believing / (D) in superstitious rituals.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb **"are believing"** is incorrect because "believe" is a stative verb and is typically not used in continuous forms.
 
• The correct form should be **"believe."**
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part C** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **C**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"It is sad that you believe in superstitious rituals."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "It is sad" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "that you"** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "in superstitious rituals."** – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **No error** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part C.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined words in the given sentence.

This newly arisen evidence __could have proved__ to finally put the culprit behind bars.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, the phrase 'newly arisen evidence could have proved' is incorrect.
 
• The word **'evidence'** is a **singular noun** and it should be followed by a **singular verb**.
 
• The correct phrase should be **'is proof'** as it correctly matches the singular noun **'evidence'**.
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase should be 'This newly arisen evidence is proof to finally put the culprit behind bars.'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 1.

Correct sentence: *This **newly arisen evidence is proof __to finally put the culprit behind bars.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The word **'proof'** is a **noun** and should be used correctly in sentences to match the context and** grammatical structure.**
 
• Ensure that the verb form matches the noun it refers to in terms of** singularity or plurality.**
 
• For example, ***'The documents are proof of his innocence.'*** Here, 'documents' is plural and matches the plural verb 'are'.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the underlined idiom in the following sentence.

Manish told Rounak __time and again__ of the ill consequences of his habit of being late to the college.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Definition:** The idiom **"time and again" **means doing something on multiple occasions, which aligns directly with the meaning of** "repeatedly."**
 
• **Context of Use: I**n the sentence, Manish warned Rounak multiple times about the consequences, indicating a repetitive action.
 
• **Synonym Fit:** **"Repeatedly"** is a synonym for** "time and again,"** meaning the same action is performed over and over.
 
• **Frequency Implication: **The idiom implies a sense of persistent effort or action, which is captured well by the word** "repeatedly."**
 
• **Consistency:** Using **"repeatedly"** maintains the sentence's original intent of emphasizing the numerous warnings given by Manish.
 
• **Common Recognition: "Repeatedly" **is a familiar and commonly understood word that accurately conveys the intended meaning of the idiom.

Therefore, the correct answer is **'Option 3'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hardly ever:** Means very rarely, which contradicts the repeated nature of the idiom.
 
• **At intervals: **Implies occasional actions at specific times, which does not capture the repetitive frequency.
 
• **Not often:** Indicating infrequent actions, which is opposite to the frequent actions implied by the idiom.

questions.solution:

__
 
• The phrase 'give away' is incorrect in this context.
 
• The correct phrasal verb to use is **'give up'**, which means to quit or stop doing something.
 
• The phrasal verbs **'give off'** and **'give out'** do not fit the context of quitting smoking.
 
 
• **Example:** If you **give up** smoking, your health will improve.
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct phrase to be used is 'give up' in place of 'give away'.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: *If you **give up** smoking, your health will improve*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The phrasal verb **'give off'** means to emit or release something.

 
 
• **Example:** *The flowers **give off** a pleasant fragrance*.
 
 
 
• The phrasal verb **'give out'** means to distribute something.
 
 
• **Example:** *The teacher **gave out** the test papers to the students*.
